newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends flat after early gains on data.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends flat after early gains on data.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended flat around C$1.3650 (US$0.7326) on Friday after drifting weaker in late trading * Canada unit strengthened earlier on weaker-than-expected U.S. producer prices * Tame February price data eased inflation fears, but markets seen jittery ahead of March 25 Fed meeting * Canada unit seen trading in narrow range next week.
The Canadian dollar finished relatively flat on Friday after surrendering its early gains on tame U.S. price data.
The Canada unit ended around C$1.3650 (US$0.7326) from Thursday's close at C$1.3653 (US$0.7324).
The currency had strengthened to C$1.3629 (US$0.7337) at midday after U.S. producer prices for February were released earlier this morning.
"We were in a bit of a defensive mode coming into the numbers. They came in weaker than expected and Canada strengthened on the back of it," one trader said.
The U.S. producer price index fell 0.4 percent in February, well below expectations for a 0.1 percent decline.
The sharper-than-expected slide in prices suggested inflation remains tame, but economists are not yet discounting a interest rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
Earlier in the week, inflation fears heightened after U.S. February retail sales came in much stronger than expected.

"The question now facing the market is not whether the Fed will tighten, but when and how much," said CIBC Wood Gundy senior economist Avery Shenfeld. Markets are weighing the odds of a rate move following a Fed meeting on March 25, he said.
Shenfeld said in a report that the odds of a March rate hike were raised by this week's data, Friday's price numbers notwithstanding.
But he continues to lean towards May as the most likely date for a Fed move..
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell to 1.2405 marks from 1.2487 marks on Thursday, but firmed to 90.36 yen from from 90.08 yen on Thursday.
